subject: Proposal: reserve floor + hot-burst credit approach for hosted API usage
messages:
From: Emma Rivera <emma@acmedata.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing alignment and burst handling

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our chat and summary pipelines. We're running an internal exercise to firm up a commercial approach and need to understand how Redwood would handle the following mix: a guaranteed monthly spend floor at a discounted rate, with frequent short spikes (hot bursts) up to 3x baseline for a few minutes at a time.

Questions we need answered before we can take this to procurement:
- If we commit to a $35k/month floor for 12 months, what per-token discount brackets apply?
- During bursts above committed throughput, how are overage rates calculated (per-token on-demand vs a separate burst uplift)?
- Can Redwood offer a small burst credit pool or a transient rate cap so we don't get penalized for brief traffic anomalies?

We can share a week of production traces if that helps. Also include any sample invoice language we'd need for procurement.

Thanks,
Emma Rivera
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Data Inc.

P.S. attaching a short CSV with our 7-day token profile for reference (acme-usage-sample.csv).

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Rivera <emma@acmedata.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing alignment and burst handling

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and thanks for the usage sample. I pulled together a concise proposal and attached a PDF with the banded discounts and a couple of alternative burst models. TL;DR:

- $35k/month committed floor (12-month term) -> 22% per-token discount off list for standard-gen text models.
- Overage handling options (pick one):
  1) On-demand per-token overage at list rate (no uplift).
  2) Hot-burst uplift model: on-demand tokens billed at list rate + 15% burst surcharge for peaks over commit for the first 30 seconds of a sustained burst; after 30s, revert to on-demand rate.
  3) Burst-credit pool: we provide 500k token burst credits per month (one-time allotment) that cover short spikes; after credits are exhausted, on-demand applies.

We typically see customers prefer option 3 for customer-facing services to avoid billing surprises — credits smooth the tail. We can also combine a small credit pool with option 2.

Attached: redwood-pricing-proposal_v2.pdf (shows invoice language and an example monthly true-up). Let me know which option you want to take to procurement and I can loop in Finance for formal language.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing alignment and burst handling — Acme deal (need quick ops/legal check)

Ben / Neha — forwarding Acme's note and the proposal I shared. Quick asks so we can respond with a recommended single path to procurement:

1) Is the 'burst-credit pool' (500k tokens/month) something we can approve at AE level for a $35k/month commit? If not, what signoff is needed?
2) If Finance wants a clearer invoice line: suggest we surface credits as "Burst Credits (monthly allotment) — non-refundable, applied before on-demand overage". Any objections?
3) Legal: does adding a transient 15% burst surcharge (option 2) require special SLA wording? My guess is no — it's a billing construct not a service penalty, but want confirmation.

I'm inclined to recommend option 3 + sample invoice language to keep procurement conversations short. Thoughts?

Karthik

Karthik — quick answers below.

1) Approvals: We can sign off on the 500k monthly burst-credit pool at AE + manager level for a $35k/month commit over 12 months. Anything larger (1M+ credits or higher dollar variance) needs Revenue Ops Director sign-off.

2) Invoice language: your suggested phrasing looks good. Recommend we also add a line: "Unused burst credits do not roll over month-to-month." That is important for procurement clarity.

3) Legal/SLA: Neha, can you confirm, but I agree with Karthik — the 15% transient surcharge is a billing construct and doesn't change SLA commitments. If Legal prefers, we can call it a "transient peak surcharge" in the billing appendix and keep the core SLA language untouched.

Neha — please flag anything I missed. If you're OK, Karthik, go ahead and send Emma a final one-pager with the recommended option (Burst-credit pool) and the invoice language; cc me and I'll prepare the draft PO terms.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
